why.headline: Organisations with Cyber Essentials certification are 92% less likely to make a cyber insurance claim than those without it.
why.caveat: This is about the certificate, not about judged: judged does not certify you and nobody has measured its effect on claims. The data is from the provider of the scheme's free insurance; it compares two groups and does not show that the certificate alone makes the difference.
why.source: UK National Cyber Security Centre, A decade of Cyber Essentials
why.quote: 92% less likely to make a cyber insurance claim
points: Collects machine evidence in all five Cyber Essentials areas: firewalls, secure configuration, user access, malware protection, updates. Linux only; its control list is not yet reviewed against the scheme.
What it could not check is never shown as passed: no permission or a missing tool is unknown, a control without machine evidence is manual.
The checks read and report; they never repair, delete or restore. Renewal, if you turn it on, runs your own ACME client.
One expiry list: certificates, keys, domains, licences and contracts with a notice period.
Secret values are never printed, only the name and file:line.
Free: MIT licence, Python, one optional dependency for notifications.
